lane's conversation, as the @{HarnessIntegration} says, so a step
        is told what the step before it did only through its prompt: the
        Chain prompt as typed and that step's final output, as the
        @{ModeSystemPrompts} says.

        In the previous tasks list, a chain's steps are grouped under one
        parent item, so they read as parts of a single chain. The parent is a
        heading row in the list, tinted the Chain colour, as the
        @{PromptModes} colours it, a little more strongly than a single
        task's tint: a joined chain icon, the first line of the prompt, and at
        its right how many steps it has, "2 steps" or "3 steps". Its status is
        the chain's as a whole, worked out only from its steps as they
        actually are, never from what the chain might still do: Running,
        with its spinner and its time counting, while one of its steps is
        building, compiling, or running now, in this project's runs, and
        while one of its steps waits in a lane's queue after an earlier step
        under way: when it finishes while a task in the other lane still
        runs, that task heads the view in its place at once, and the task
        that finished goes among the previous tasks. So with two Chain tasks
        sent one after the other, once both their spec steps have finished,
        the first chain's code step heads the view while it runs, not the
        second chain's finished spec step, and the second chain's code step
        heads it in turn once it is sent. A task still running in the other
        lane that is not the latest is among the previous tasks, shown
        running there, as any previous task is. Whichever task heads the
        view, its header and output show as they do for a task just sent,
        and the previous tasks, their row's count, and the chain grouping

        previous tasks row and the queue shows its conversation as a chat, in
        place of the latest task's header and output table. The chat holds
        the latest task and the Freeform tasks sent straight before it, back
        to the last task of another mode, or to the first that started a new

    previousTasks:
        Among the previous tasks, a Freeform task keeps its heading like any
        task's, tinted grey, and opens onto its prompt and its reply laid out
        as they are in the chat, rather than a compiled prompt and a table.

content.text:
Possibly, yes: several of my recent spec changes moved how previous tasks are viewed, and some older text still described the old way. I can't see the running app from this step, so I can't confirm what's broken there. These spec changes are the likeliest causes:

- **Chat tab:** it now only shows running tasks, or the last one that finished. Previous tasks don't appear there any more.
- **Where to find them:** the right sidebar's Tasks tab, in its "Previous" section. That section starts collapsed every time a project opens, so it can look as if they're gone.
- **Opening one:** clicking a previous task opens its details in the sidebar and its output in a tab of its own in the body.

**Contradictions I cleaned up:**
- The old "previous tasks row", which no longer exists.
- Chains described as an indented group with checkboxes instead of a single row.
- Running tasks said to be listed among the previous tasks.
- Rows tinted whole instead of marked by their mode-coloured bar.

**What the spec now says plainly:** every previous task opens and can be read in full, whatever its status or age, while its record is in the history. A record that can't be read still opens, with a muted note saying why.

`piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 84 files.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `TasksTab` `#rows` and `#details`, `Body` `#task-tabs`, `PromptEditor` `#previous-tasks`, `#chained-tasks` and `#header`, and `MessageList` `#freeform` and `#backgrounds`. If you can tell me what you see when you try to open one, I can narrow it down.
